title: Qualitative Study to Develop a Pilot Information Course about Back Pain
summary: Negative, often outdated biomedical, beliefs about back pain are related to negative clinical outcomes. Addressing these negative beliefs and misconception is supposed to reduce disability and pain. The aim should not merely be to provide information, but to encourage people to understand and apply that knowledge. In this study, an information course addressing prevalent misconceptions about back pain should be developed and presented to focusgroups. The group should subsequently discuss the course. The results of this discussion should enable the researchers to revise the informational course to fit the needs and wishes of the participants.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Ability to speak and understand German language fluently to participate in the focusgroup.
Exclusion criteria:
Serious health issues like tumors, fractures, infections, cauda equina syndrome, axial spondylarthritis, recent surgery or pregnancy.
